state:
An OpenTofu (Terraform) plan is about to be applied to live infrastructure on one server: Docker containers and volumes, and a PostgreSQL server whose databases are used by running applications. Applying the plan carries out the resource changes below in dependency order. Replacing a resource destroys the old one and then creates the new one, unless the plan says the new one is created first (create_before_destroy). If a change fails, the apply stops there; the changes already made stay made.

Current state:
docker_container.db: container tfg-s22-db, image postgres:17-alpine, running; publishes 127.0.0.1:47088 -> 5432/tcp (answering); environment: PGDATA=/var/lib/postgresql/data, POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(secret); named volume tfg-s22-data mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data (39 MB)
docker_volume.data: volume tfg-s22-data (39 MB), used by tfg-s22-db

Actions, in order:
1. Replace docker_container.db (destroy the old one, then create the new one, forced by the change to env): env: ["POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(secret)"] -> ["POSTGRES_PASSWORD=(secret)", "TZ=UTC"]; volumes: {container_path = "/var/lib/postgresql/data", read_only = false, volume_name = "tfg-s22-data"} -> {container_path = "/var/lib/postgresql/data", volume_name = "tfg-s22-data"}

How these providers behave: Destroying a Docker container also deletes its anonymous volumes; a named volume or a host directory mounted into it is kept unless that volume is destroyed too. A new container starts from its image: files the old one wrote outside its named volumes and host directories are not in it. Docker refuses to create a container whose name, or published host port, is already in use, and the change fails. The postgres image applies POSTGRES_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD only when it initializes an empty data directory; a data directory that already holds a database keeps its users and pg_hba.conf. A Docker port published with ip 0.0.0.0 (or with no ip) is reachable from every network the server is on; with ip 127.0.0.1 only from the server itself.

The questions are about the state after all these actions.
